teach_en: Every Lao word has a melody: your voice rises, falls or stays level as you say it. ເຂົ້າ (rice) and ເຂົ່າ (knee) have the same letters and the same sounds. Only the small tone mark on top is different: ◌້ on rice, ◌່ on knee. That mark changes the melody, and the melody alone makes them two different words. The line next to each word is a picture of its melody: where your voice starts and ends, high or low in the box. Play each word and copy its melody. || W000019 || W000724

teach_en: The same mark ◌້ sits on ເຂົ້າ (rice) and on ນ້ຳ (water), but their melodies are different. A mark does not give one fixed melody, so listen to each word and learn its melody with it. || W000019 || W000011 || W000562
notes: Recap (LESSON_RULES decision 18; PLAN L3 from the November review): ◌້ gives low-falling on ເຂົ້າ (high-class ຂ) and high-falling on ນ້ຳ (low-class ນ), per tone_derive. Class is named only in this note, not on the card.

teach_en: ມາ (come) has no tone mark. ມ້າ (horse) has the mark ◌້. The sounds are the same: the mark changes the melody. Play both and hear the difference. || W000025 || W000562
